That sits at the midpoint of the company's $4.33-4.79 / $1.90-1.98B guide, with a $4.80 whisper. Aggregators disagree on full-year FY27 EPS: MarketBeat says $15.89, which implies about $1.62 for Q4, while an undated post-Q2 Zacks figure of $17.19 implies about $2.86. FY28 is about $20 (Zacks), so the stock trades near 11x FY28 consensus, which suggests the price already assumes cuts. view: Dycom has beaten consensus EPS in 8 of its last 8 quarters and cleared the top of its own guide by a wide margin twice this year: $4.42 against a $2.57-2.90 guide, then $5.29 against $4.40-4.82. A Q3 beat is the base case, and the $4.80 whisper already holds it. As in August, the reaction will turn on the Q4 guide and how management talks about FY28: wireless timing, AT&T's lower 2027-28 capital plan, Verizon's capex discipline, the Lumen fiber assets moving into the AT&T/GIP/CPP joint venture, and whether the hyperscaler long-haul and data-center work survives the moratorium politics. The counterparty evidence since August leans negative. MasTec's communications revenue fell to $807M from $915M and its communications backlog fell from June to September, on customer deferrals, customer reorganisations and fourth-carrier uncertainty. AT&T trimmed its capital plan and cited construction efficiencies, which pressures cost per passing. Verizon's nine-month capex is below last year even with Frontier included. But each of these hit DY's price on the day it came out, so I cannot call them unpriced. On the other side the bar looks low: 59% off the high, about 11x FY28 consensus, sentiment 'barely positive', a brokerage target cut to $300 just before the print, and rising shorts. A beat with the full-year guide held and record backlog could produce a relief move. A fresh wireless deferral or a Q4 guide under the Street would repeat August. The FY guide arithmetic (FY midpoint $7.57B less H1 $3.97B less Q3 midpoint $1.94B leaves about $1.66B for Q4) makes a seasonally soft Q4 likely, and I cannot pin the true Q4 EPS consensus because the aggregators disagree by more than $1. The day's sector beta (moves of 5-12% in peers on macro AI headlines) will add noise inside the 13:00 window. Net: no edge I can show. Washed-out positioning and the beat record tilt slightly up, and the counterparty deferrals tilt down.

recommendation.reason: The negatives I found all have dated price moves tied to them: AT&T's capital-plan cut, MasTec's communications deferrals and the data-center moratorium selloff. The positive is DY's habit of beating the top of its guide, and the whisper already holds that. The deciding line is the Q4 guide and the FY28 tone. Since the true Q4 consensus is ambiguous across aggregators, I cannot show which side of the real bar the guide will land on. With no mechanism the price has missed, there is no recommendation.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A cut to the FY27 communications revenue range or another wireless/AT&T deferral (would make it a clear short), or the full-year guide held with record backlog and confident FY28 hyperscaler/BEAD commentary (would make it a relief long).

self_critique: The case for down: Dycom shares its customers with MasTec, and MasTec's communications backlog fell from June to September on deferrals. AT&T, DY's largest customer, cut its forward capital plan and talks about construction efficiencies. If the published consensus still sits near the higher Zacks figure, any honest Q4 guide that reflects these deferrals lands below it, which is exactly the August pattern (beat, guide below consensus, -11.6%). The case for up: the stock already prices FY28 at about 11x after a 59% fall, and a beat with backlog growth could cause a sharp short-covering move. Either case is plausible, and neither shows me something the price has not seen.
approach_notes: P4 ('priced in is a claim to prove') helped most: tying each negative datapoint to a dated DY price move, against a peer that moved the other way, is what kept me from shorting on the MasTec read-through. P3's counterparty route paid. The consensus ambiguity between aggregators is a gap the playbook does not address: it needs a way to settle the true bar when sources disagree by more than $1.
